steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Arousal: A state of physical and psychological readiness and activation. It is the level of excitement, alertness and energy a performer experiences. Arousal exists on a continuum from deep sleep (very low) to extreme excitement or panic (very high). | Inverted-U Theory (Yerkes-Dodson Law): The theory that performance improves as arousal increases, but only up to an optimal point. Beyond this point, further increases in arousal lead to a decline in performance. When graphed, this relationship forms an inverted U shape. | Zone of Optimal Functioning (ZOF): Each individual performer has their own personal zone of optimal arousal where they perform at their best. steps.body: Define arousal and explain how it affects sporting performance using the inverted-U theory. | Explain why a rugby player needs a higher optimal arousal level than a snooker player. | Describe three stress management techniques a performer can use to reduce over-arousal.
